subject: 2 basics questions about Rmarkdown from RStudio

messages.author: 605c14114b1f1179
messages.subject: 2 basics questions about Rmarkdown from RStudio
parts:
Hello...

First, i would like to express how impressed i am with the ability and ease to create webcontent (HTML files) from within RStudio, using tools like Knitr, and markdown...

The Markdown reference in Rstudio is very good, allowed me to create useful notes for myself and to share with colleagues, which is great. However i had two basic questions which i was not able to find answers to, and so i am hoping someone on this group might be able to help

1) Is there a way to underlying a text, similar to the way _word_ would make the word italic
2) I am trying to create reference within the document, in such a way that if that if a reader press on [linked word], it would take him to another part of the document. Similar to the way the link to a website works, but instead of a weblink, it would be a link to another part of the document

I thought the solution to the second question would be, as described in the Markdown reference page:

A [linked phrase][id]. 

At the bottom of the document:

[id]: http://example.com/ "Title"

But that didn't work. So if that is the correct way, can someone provide a simpler example.

Thank you in advance.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] 2 basics questions about Rmarkdown from RStudio
parts:
1. the answer can be very long or very short; you can say <u></u>, but
others may say it is a bad idea; for example, here is a discussion:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2110779/is-use-of-uunderline-u-deprecated-and-non-validated

2. whenever you realize you cannot do something in Markdown, remember
you always have HTML, and Markdown understands HTML; it is trivial to
create anchors in HTML, and again, HTML is too flexible to give you
one single answer, e.g. http://help.typepad.com/anchor-tags.html
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/484719/html-anchors-with-name-or-id

so your "basic" questions are not basic -- they require you to learn
the giant behind markdown, i.e. HTML (fortunately, HTML is a very
simple language as well)

Regards,
Yihui
